title: Acoustic Insulation Lining in the Fwd Cabin Divider Bays
abstract: An absorbent lining is proposed for the void above and behind the forward cabin dividers, to remove the measured sound level step between the divider seat rows and the rest of the premium cabin.

sections.reason: One operator has logged sixty-one written passenger complaints in a year, all naming the two seat rows either side of the forward divider, and its own cruise measurements show a four decibel step against a reference position eight rows aft. Divider panel seal replacement on two aircraft produced no measurable change. Our own survey on a company aircraft reproduces the step and traces it to the open void above the divider panel line, where the ceiling treatment stops short and the panel acts as a reflector into the seat rows rather than as a barrier.
sections.description: An absorbent lining is fitted into the void above and behind the forward divider panels, dressed to the existing panel line so that no cabin dimension changes. The divider trim D2520138833226 is replaced by a version with a deeper return that captures the lining edge, and the adjacent passenger compartment trim D2520000645001 is re-shimmed by 4 mm so that the two panel lines still meet. Floating barrel nuts AES161226K4 in the existing hard points carry the lining frame; no new attachment into structure is created. Work is in the forward cabin and ceiling void, zones 221, 291 and 222, with the divider panels and the adjacent ceiling panels removed. The curtain rail 280DL is removed and refitted, and the partition 39DL9 is unchanged apart from a new sealing strip at its upper edge.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 9 kg per aircraft in the forward cabin. No electrical load change. Interchangeable, and the lining can be removed without trace if an operator reconfigures the cabin. The predicted improvement is 3 to 4 decibels at the affected rows, which closes the step. No change to seat count, to stowage volume or to the certified exit arrangement, but the lining sits close to the cabin emergency marking run and the clearance has to be proven. Cabin cleaning access to the void is unchanged.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, during a scheduled cabin visit, estimated at one shift with three people per aircraft. The candidate population is the five aircraft named by the requesting operator; a wider offer would follow if the measured improvement is confirmed on the first embodiment.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm the clearance between the lining frame and the cabin floor proximity marking installation, establish whether the flammability substantiation of the existing lining family can be extended to this application, and check whether an equivalent treatment already exists elsewhere in the aircraft that could simply be re-used.

type_data.balance_impact: Forward cabin, CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in proposed; customer option only if the measured benefit is confirmed
